result.title: REDAR: Reinforcement-Driven Adaptive Regularisation for Class Incremental Learning
result.comment: The 28th International Conference on Digital Image Computing: Techniques and Applications (DICTA 2026)
result.summary: Regularisation-based class-incremental learning (CIL) methods control the stability-plasticity trade-off through fixed coefficients tuned offline, independently of the continual learning objective and blind to phase-specific variations in data volume, task difficulty, and class similarity. We argue this is a fundamental mismatch and propose REDAR: Reinforcement-Driven Adaptive Regularisation for Class Incremental Learning, which treats regularisation strength selection as a sequential decision problem. At each incremental phase, a lightweight reinforcement learning (RL) agent observes a compact state of current performance metrics and incoming data statistics, and outputs the distillation coefficients for that phase. To respect CIL's constraint on historical data access, the policy is trained entirely on pseudo-CIL tasks constructed from the initial phase, then deployed on the incremental sequence without further adaptation. Experiments on CIFAR-100 and Tiny-ImageNet demonstrate that REDAR reduces forgetting and improves forward transfer over fixed and heuristic baselines, and that policies trained on short pseudo-task horizons transfer effectively to longer incremental runs.

AI.brief_summary: 针对类增量学习中固定正则化系数难以适配不同阶段的问题，提出 REDAR：用轻量 RL 智能体根据当前性能指标与数据统计输出每阶段的蒸馏系数，并在初始阶段构造的伪增量任务上训练策略后直接部署。在 CIFAR-100 与 Tiny-ImageNet 上报告遗忘减少、前向迁移提升，且短伪任务训练的策略可迁移到更长序列。
AI.relevance_reason: 与视觉推理主线关联较弱，但「由紧凑状态驱动的策略调控标量控制量」以及「短视界策略迁移到长序列」可供核查是否能类比 LVR 中的动态计算分配、停止决策与长度泛化。
